candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis specifies negative pressure pulmonary oedema caused by forceful inspiratory effort against a blocked airway (compacted snow), combined with pulmonary haemorrhage. HAPE is a separate pathophysiological entity driven by hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction at altitude. Although the incident occurred at 2500 m, the clinical picture (acute onset during burial, haemoptysis, rapid resolution, normal echo/BNP, no prior altitude acclimatisation issue) and mechanism (airway obstruction causing extreme negative intrathoracic pressure) are inconsistent with HAPE. C001 asserts an incompatible etiology and omits the haemorrhage component.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: HAPE is a distinct altitude-related etiology; reference requires negative pressure (obstructive/Mueller maneuver) mechanism plus pulmonary haemorrhage component

case_quality_flags: Altitude of 2500 m is below the typical HAPE threshold (>2500–3000 m), further supporting negative pressure mechanism over HAPE
Haemoptysis and bilateral infiltrates with normal BNP/troponin and rapid resolution are hallmarks of negative pressure pulmonary oedema with haemorrhage, not HAPE
